headline: A second wave of AI spending doubt, triggered by Meta's negative free cash flow and Tesla's capex cut, knocked the Nasdaq down 2.60 percent and the Philadelphia semiconductor index 6.7 percent, dragged the Kospi 3.5 percent and the Nikkei 2.65 percent lower, and pushed the US 10 year yield below 5 percent even as Brent cleared 112 dollars on reported tanker damage in the Strait of Hormuz.

summary.us: The S&P 500 fell 1.21 percent to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite 2.60 percent to 26,008.86 while the Dow finished flat at 52,867.98, as Meta dropped close to 7 percent on negative third quarter free cash flow and a full year capital spending floor raised to 135 billion to 145 billion dollars, and Lam Research's supply chain warning sent the Philadelphia semiconductor index down 6.7 percent for its worst day since June. Tesla beat on adjusted earnings of 48 cents and posted 1.53 billion dollars of free cash flow but cut 2026 capex to about 20 billion dollars, the 10 year Treasury yield fell about 19 basis points to 4.95 percent, its biggest one day drop since August 2025, and Apple closed at a record 348.22 dollars even as Loop Capital downgraded it to Hold.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 fell 0.54 percent to 22,687.65 and the Sensex 460.30 points to 73,249.39 for a third straight decline, with Bank Nifty almost flat at 54,925.70 as HDFC Bank lost 1.82 percent and ICICI Bank gained, while breadth was weak at 940 advances against 2,540 declines. Brent above 112 dollars and Middle East tension drove the selling in energy, FMCG and IT, foreign investors sold 3,458.70 crore rupees against domestic buying of 2,891.32 crore rupees, the rupee snapped an eight session winning run to settle near 94.83 a dollar, and the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO was subscribed about 5.2 times by the end of day two with institutions near 12 times.
summary.global: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1,713.40 points or 2.65 percent to 62,907.84, its lowest close since July 30, and Korea's Kospi dropped 3.52 percent to 5,533.77 as Samsung Electronics lost 4.03 percent and SK hynix 5.49 percent on doubts about returns across the AI investment chain. Alibaba posted its steepest fall in two months and the Hang Seng Tech Index closed 5 percent lower after Chinese authorities summoned e-commerce operators over product quality standards, Europe closed broadly red with the DAX down 1.07 percent and the CAC 40 down 1.39 percent, and copper slid 1.8 percent to a five week low of 14,089 dollars a tonne on a fourth straight day of LME inventory builds.

calendar.what: Infosys September quarter results at 3:45pm IST with a board decision on an interim dividend, on an Indian earnings day of roughly 61 companies that also includes Dr Reddy's Laboratories, JSW Steel, Tata Motors, IndusInd Bank, Bharat Petroleum and Coforge; Jio Platforms IPO closes; EAAA India Alternatives anchor book; Apple foldable iPhone Duo goes on sale in stores
EAAA India Alternatives IPO opens at a price band of 1,585 to 1,665 rupees for a 1,200 crore rupee offer for sale; Jio Platforms allotment expected
US Federal Open Market Committee two day meeting begins; US consumer confidence at 10:00am New York time; SFC Environmental Technologies and BLS Polymers IPOs open in India

Fed decision at 2:00pm New York time with a press conference at 2:30pm and no Summary of Economic Projections, with markets putting the odds of a move at this meeting near 10 percent; Microsoft and Alphabet September quarter results; Adani Enterprises and Adani Ports board meetings on results; EAAA India Alternatives IPO closes; Jio Platforms listing expected

US advance third quarter GDP, September PCE and weekly jobless claims at 8:30am New York time; Amazon results; Bank of Japan two day meeting begins; SFC Environmental Technologies and BLS Polymers IPOs close

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
